messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
the instruments disagree by small amounts that matter to the conclusion while you are handling Two explanations for an unfamiliar failure. You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "the instruments disagree. the wrench taps my thigh. i press the edge with the other. the explanation says the key was loose under the bench. the second says the old one. i press the old one harder. the key stays loose. the two explanations clash. i tap the bench with the old one, then the new one. the two sparks. i listen to the new one. the old one says the key is under the bench. the conclusion says the old one is the one that breaks."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "I turn the two pieces between finger and thumb. One edge catches, then drops. I hold the smaller one against the cloth and leave the other alone. The difference feels smaller than the argument."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i keep the two explanations side by the edge and mark the instrument with ‘not clear.’ i fold the paper and write ‘not clear’ on the other side. i trust the edge case and keep the second one until the end."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i tap the table edge twice with my fingertip, then hold the two pieces apart and write the difference beside the failure. “the second one,” i say, and tap the paper with my fingertip once. “i keep the first in my pocket.” i leave the explanation behind and write the instrument name beside the failure on the table edge."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I stop and look at the two explanations. small amounts. one is the same, but the other is different. i put the smaller one in my pocket and pocket the larger one, but not yet. i test the smaller one with a rusted bolt, then leave it in the failure. the difference stays in the failure. the conclusion is still the same, but the small thing is waiting to be seen."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i hold one instrument near the door and fold the paper with the other. the paper changes shape, so i fold the other one. the two explanations say the same thing, so i fold one into my palm and leave the other aside. the fold has become a story now. i keep folding until one of them fits my hand."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I mark the mismatched contact with grease and leave it that way. I run one short test with one fresh stick, then leave the old explanation beside the bench. I keep the scratched edge beside the bench, leave the mismatched stick beside the bench, and watch where it catches."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "1. check the small amounts. 2. one watch: slow. 3. check the line. 4. check the square. 5. i keep it tidy. 6. ask the watch for the date. 7. one small mark. 8. i write it down. 9. test the small mark. 10. check the watch. slow. 11. keep it simple."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i move the two pieces slowly and keep the one I leave behind. i write the difference on a loose sketchbook page and keep the other in my pocket. i wait for the other to stop moving."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i hold the two explanations apart and trace the edge with my thumbnail. “the smaller one catches first,” i say, stopping when i find a faint scratch that feels like a tiny screw. “the other one keeps moving.” i leave the old one beside the instrument and watch the key stick move when i tap it once."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i write the small amount on the test sheet, then check the explanation. i say sorry to the instrument, then leave it alone. i photograph the fault, then write the verdict on the test sheet. i keep the two explanations separate and leave the one that matters."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "the gap widens. i touch the wrench against my thigh, then stop. “one,” i say, though the other says no. i lean closer again, then stop again."}]
